problem: Visual navigation lacks real-world human-navigation datasets that support supervised learning of human-centric exploration policies (waypoint prediction) and that carry landmark annotations for map/graph building and localization. Existing datasets (Habitat-Web, RUGD, SCAND, etc.) have no landmark labels.
motivation: Image-goal navigation success depends on efficient exploration, but existing methods either assume the environment was pre-seen, hard-code exploration, or need costly RL or ground-truth semantics. Humans navigate by treating landmarks as nodes in a mental graph, so human point-click waypoints plus landmark labels could supervise simpler networks and topological map learning.
key_idea: Release LAVN, a dataset of human-guided exploration videos in Habitat (Gibson and Matterport) and real-world scenes, with per-step human point-click waypoints and annotated landmarks, plus RGBD, odometry and action sequences.
insight: This is a dataset paper with no experiments or ablations, so there are no empirical insights. The design claim is that dense human click supervision (maskable to temporally abstracted waypoints) plus sparse landmarks can act as graph nodes, linking supervised waypoint prediction and contrastive map representation learning. Real-world data is collected under the same protocol as simulation to keep the two consistent.
method: Virtual collection: a human navigator in Habitat-Sim (Gibson and Matterport scenes) left-clicks the first-person view to move (forward 0.25 m, turn ±15°) and right-clicks to mark landmarks; trajectories end after 500 actions or full coverage.

Graph representation: each step is a node with RGB, depth, click point and GT odometry (location and orientation); edges link consecutive nodes; the action list and landmark (coordinate, node) pairs are stored in worker_graph.json.

Real-world collection: an iPhone 13 mini held about 1.5 m high, with a photo per step (about 0.7 m) or per turn (about 15°), following the same protocol; waypoints and landmarks are annotated offline; images resized from 4032x3024 to 640x480 JPEG.
Scene selection: rooms are sampled evenly by scene ID across Gibson (A–Z) and Matterport (000–007) for diversity in type and size; trajectories with incorrect labels are removed.
Proposed uses: supervised RGBD-to-waypoint regression, and contrastive map representation learning where nearby nodes are positives and landmarks give global structure.

setting.training_data: n/a; dataset of 310 trajectories, 103,998 frames, 14,281 landmarks, 300 virtual and 10 real environments
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (virtual and real) plus depth (virtual only), with GT odometry in simulation
setting.action_space: discrete: move forward 0.25 m, turn left 15°, turn right 15° (real world approximated by human judgement); human point-click waypoints in image coordinates
setting.simulator: Habitat-Sim (Gibson and Matterport scenes) plus real-world captures
setting.privileged: none (GT odometry provided as data in simulation)

numbers_note: Dataset paper with no benchmark results reported; only dataset statistics.
results: The paper introduces LAVN with 310 trajectories, 103,998 frames and 14,281 landmarks across 300 virtual and 10 real environments. It reports no model performance results; statistics are given as histograms and a table, and trajectory lengths range from 1.16 m to 85.38 m.
limitations: No baselines or experiments demonstrating the dataset's benefit; the claims are only intuited.
Small real-world portion (10 scenes), with inexact human-held camera motion, no depth, and no dynamic objects; no recommended train/val split.
Landmark definition is subjective (annotated by the authors only).
